column1: # Fighter-owned effects that get a RESIDENT STAND-IN instead of being dropped.
# ADR 0002 forbids requesting another fighter's effect archive, and tools/extract-effects.awk
# enforces it by keeping only `sys_*` spawns. That is correct and stays. What it cannot distinguish
# is a decorative effect from a LOAD-BEARING one: Wolf's f-air is a claw swipe whose reach is only
# legible from the arc it draws, so dropping the arc does not merely make the move plainer, it makes
# it unreadable -- the playtest report was "needs a visual so the user knows how far the move is
# going".
# THE ADR WARNED ABOUT THE OTHER DIRECTION, and this is not that. Its prediction was that a future
# reader would "fix" the generic visuals by wiring up the real fighter-prefixed names, which compile,
# deploy and silently do nothing on a card without that fighter. A substitution names a `sys_`
# archive, which is always resident, so gate 4o still passes by construction -- the check is that
# the REPLACEMENT is `sys_*`, not that nothing was replaced.
# EVERY OTHER ARGUMENT IS CARRIED OVER UNCHANGED. The effect name is the only thing swapped: the
# joint, the offsets, the RGB and the scale are the source's own numbers, so the stand-in is drawn
# where, and in the colour, the real one was. Wolf's arc is (0, 0, 250) -- pure blue -- and it stays
# pure blue.
# ADD A ROW ONLY WITH A REASON IN THE THIRD COLUMN, and only when the effect carries information the
# player needs. A substitution is still not the real effect, and a screen full of `sys_attack_arc`
# standing in for six different fighters' signature visuals would be worse than six plain moves.
# source effect <TAB> sys_ stand-in <TAB> why this one earns a stand-in
wolf_scratch_arc
column3: Wolf's f-air: the arc is the only thing on screen that shows how far the swipe reaches, and the move read as having no hitbox without it
